intro: Thailand is a constitutional monarchy, but the army and the palace have long played big roles in politics.

chapters.title: How it works
text: The king is head of state and deeply respected; criticising him is a crime. The prime minister leads the government, chosen by an elected House of Representatives. Anutin Charnvirakul of the Bhumjaithai party led his party to victory in the February 2026 election. Voters also backed writing a new constitution.
Thailand has had around 20 constitutions since 1932 and a dozen successful coups.

chapters.title: Protests and politics
text: Rival 'Red Shirt' and 'Yellow Shirt' movements clashed in the 2000s and 2010s. In 2020 young people led big protests calling for reform.

keyTerms.meaning: A king or queen reigns, but laws are made by an elected parliament.
